paragraphs: Beacon Financial Corporation, a Delaware corporation, is the holding company for Beacon Bank & Trust and its subsidiaries and Clarendon Private.

The Company offers a wide range of commercial, business and retail banking services, including a full complement of cash management products, foreign exchange services, on-line and mobile banking services, consumer and residential loans and wealth management services. Clarendon Private is a registered investment advisor with the SEC. Through Clarendon Private and the Trust and Investments Division of the Bank, the Company offers a wide range of wealth management services to individuals, families, endowments and foundations to help these clients meet their long-term financial goals.

As a full-service financial institution with 147 banking offices throughout New England and New York, the Bank and its subsidiaries focus their efforts on developing and deepening long-term banking relationships with qualified customers through a full complement of products, excellent customer service, and strong risk management.
The Company's headquarters and executive management are located at 131 Clarendon Street, Boston, Massachusetts 02116, and its telephone number is 617-425-4600.

On September 1, 2025, the Company completed its merger of equals with Brookline Bancorp, Inc. ("Legacy Brookline"), pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of December 16, 2024, by and among the Company, Commerce Acquisition Sub, Inc. and Legacy Brookline (the "Merger Agreement"). On September 1, 2025, Commerce Acquisition Sub, Inc. merged with and into Legacy Brookline (the "Merger"), immediately followed by the merger of Legacy Brookline with and

into the Company (the "Holdco Merger"), with the Company as the resulting corporation. The Company also changed its name from Berkshire Hills Bancorp, Inc. to Beacon Financial Corporation and changed the New York Stock Exchange ticker symbol for its common stock from "BHLB" to "BBT."

Immediately following the Holdco Merger, Berkshire Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Bank Rhode Island, a wholly owned subsidiary of Legacy Brookline, and PCSB Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary of Legacy Brookline, each merged with and into Brookline Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary of Legacy Brookline, with Brookline Bank as the surviving bank (the "Bank Mergers" and, together with the Merger and the Holdco Merger, the "Transaction"). In connection with the Bank Mergers, Brookline Bank changed its name to Beacon Bank & Trust.

The Transaction was treated as a business combination under ASC 805 and was accounted for as a reverse merger using the acquisition method of accounting. Therefore, Legacy Brookline was deemed the acquirer for financial reporting purposes even though Legacy Berkshire was the legal acquirer. As such, the historical financial statements of Legacy Brookline became the historical financial statements of the combined company.

The loan and lease portfolio increased $8.3 billion, or 84.4%, to $18.0 billion at December 31, 2025 from $9.8 billion at December 31, 2024. The Company's commercial loan portfolios, which totaled $14.0 billion, or 77.4% of total loans and leases, as of December 31, 2025, increased $5.7 billion, or 69.8%, from $8.2 billion, or 84.1% of total loans and leases, as of December 31, 2024.

Total deposits increased $10.6 billion, or 119.2%, to $19.5 billion at December 31, 2025 from $8.9 billion as of December 31, 2024. Core deposits, which include demand checking, NOW, non-payroll money market and savings accounts, increased 112.6% to $13.1 billion as of December 31, 2025 from $6.1 billion at December 31, 2024. The Company's core deposits were 67.0% of total deposits at December 31, 2025, a decrease from 69.1% at December 31, 2024.

The Bank also operates a commercial payment processing business that serves regional and national payroll service bureau customers. These payroll deposits, included in money market often fluctuate daily by hundreds of millions of dollars depending on payroll cycles. Payroll deposits, included in money market accounts in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets, totaled $1.9 billion as of December 31, 2025, all of which was assumed in the Transaction.

The allowance for loan and lease losses increased $127.8 million, or 102.1%, to $252.8 million as of December 31, 2025 from $125.1 million as of December 31, 2024. The ratio of the allowance for loan and lease losses to total loans and leases was 1.40% as of December 31, 2025 compared to 1.28% as of December 31, 2024. Nonperforming assets as of December 31, 2025 were $116.7 million, up from $70.5 million at the end of 2024. Nonperforming assets were 0.50% and 0.59% of total assets as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively.

Net interest income increased $173.5 million, or 52.6%, to $503.1 million in 2025 compared to $329.6 million in 2024. Net interest margin increased 50 basis points to 3.56% in 2025 from 3.06% in 2024. Net income for 2025 increased $21.6 million, or 31.4%, to $90.3 million from $68.7 million for 2024. Basic and fully diluted earnings per common share ("EPS") increased to $1.03 for 2025 from $0.77 for 2024. See Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."

The Company is subject to strong competition from banks and other financial institutions and financial service providers. The Company faces considerable competition from banking and non-banking organizations, including traditional banks, online banks, financial technology companies, wealth management companies and others, in its market area for all aspects of banking and related service activities. Competitive factors considered for loan generation include product offerings, interest rates, terms offered, services provided and geographic locations. Competitive factors considered in attracting and retaining deposits include product offerings and rate of return, convenient branch locations and automated teller machines and online access to accounts.

headings: Changes to interest rates could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.
We may be adversely affected by volatility in U.S. and global economic conditions and changes in fiscal, monetary, trade and regulatory policies.
Inflation can have an adverse impact on our business and on our customers.
Our business may be adversely affected by changes in economic conditions in our market area.
If we are unable to access the capital markets, have prolonged net deposit outflows, or our borrowing costs increase, our liquidity and competitive position will be negatively affected.
We face significant and increasing competition in the financial services industry.
Development of new products services and technologies may impose additional costs on us and may expose us to increased operational risk.
Changes in U.S. trade policies, including the imposition of tariffs and retaliatory tariffs, may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
If our allowance for credit losses is not sufficient to cover actual loan and lease losses, our earnings may decrease.
Our loan and lease portfolios include commercial real estate mortgage loans and commercial loans and leases, including equipment leases, which are generally riskier than other types of loans.

A portion of our loan portfolio consists of loan participations, which may have a higher risk of loss than loans we originate because we are not the lead lender and we have limited control over credit monitoring.
We are subject to a variety of risks in connection with any sale of loans we may conduct.
44 Business Capital's SBA 7(a) lending program business is dependent upon the U.S. federal government, and we face specific risks associated with originating SBA loans.
Environmental liability associated with our lending activities could result in losses.
The fair value of our investment securities can fluctuate due to factors outside of our control.
Potential downgrades of U.S. government securities by one or more of the credit ratings agencies could have a material adverse effect on our operations, earnings, and financial condition.
Loss of deposits or a change in deposit mix could increase our cost of funding.
Wholesale funding sources may prove insufficient to replace deposits at maturity and support our operations and future growth.
Potential deterioration in the performance or financial position of the FHLB might restrict our funding needs and may adversely impact our financial condition and results of operations.
The soundness of other financial institutions could adversely affect us.
Our ability to service our debt and pay dividends is dependent on capital distributions from the Bank, and these distributions are subject to regulatory limits and other restrictions.
Damage to our reputation could significantly harm our business, including our competitive position and business prospects.
We may be unable to attract and retain qualified key employees, which could adversely affect our business prospects, including our competitive position and results of operations.
We face continuing and growing security risks to our data, including the information we maintain relating to our customers.
We may not be able to successfully implement future information technology system enhancements, which could adversely affect our business operations and profitability.
We rely on other companies to provide key components of our business infrastructure.
We may incur significant losses as a result of ineffective risk management processes and strategies.
Our internal controls, procedures and policies may fail or be circumvented.
Changes in tax laws and regulations and differences in interpretation of tax laws and regulations may adversely impact our financial statements.
Natural disasters, acts of terrorism, future pandemics and other external events could harm our business.
Our financial statements are based in part on assumptions and estimates, which, if wrong, could cause unexpected losses in the future.
Changes in accounting standards can be difficult to predict and can materially impact how we record and report our financial condition and results of operations.
We may be required to write down goodwill and other acquisition-related identifiable intangible assets.
We operate in a highly regulated industry, and laws and regulations, or changes in them, could limit or restrict our activities and could have a material adverse effect on our operations.

We are subject to numerous laws designed to protect consumers, including the Community Reinvestment Act and fair lending laws, and failure to comply with these laws could lead to a wide variety of sanctions.
We may become subject to enforcements actions even though noncompliance was inadvertent or unintentional.
We face significant legal risks, both from regulatory investigations and proceedings and from private actions brought against us.
The FRB may require us to commit capital resources to support the Bank.
We are subject to stringent capital requirements which may adversely impact return on equity, require additional capital raises, or limit the ability to pay dividends or repurchase shares.
We may fail to realize the anticipated benefits of the Transaction.
We may be unable to retain personnel successfully following the Transaction.
paragraphs: Before deciding to invest in us or deciding to maintain or increase your investment, you should carefully consider the risks described below, in addition to the other information contained in this report and in our other filings with the SEC. The risks and uncertainties described below and in our other filings are not the only ones facing us. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our business. If any of these known or unknown risks or uncertainties actually occur, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be seriously harmed. In that event, the market price for our common stock could decline and you may lose your investment.
RISKS RELATED TO OUR BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY

Our consolidated results of operations depend in large part on net interest income, which is the difference between (i) interest income on interest-earning assets, such as loans, leases and securities, and (ii) interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities, such as deposits and borrowed funds. As a result, our earnings and growth are significantly affected by interest rates, which are subject to the influence of economic conditions generally, both domestic and foreign, to events in the capital markets, and also to the monetary and fiscal policies of the U.S. and the FRB. The nature and timing of any changes in such policies and their effect on us cannot be controlled and are extremely difficult to predict. An increase in interest rates could also have a negative impact on our results of operations by reducing the ability of borrowers to repay their current loan obligations, which could not only result in increased loan defaults, foreclosures, and charge-offs, but also necessitate further increases to our allowances for loan losses. A decrease in interest rates may trigger loan prepayments, which may serve to reduce net interest income if we are unable to lend those funds to other borrowers or invest the funds at the same or higher interest rates.

The economy in the U.S. and globally has experienced volatility in recent years and may continue to experience such volatility for the foreseeable future. Unfavorable or uncertain economic conditions can be caused by declines in economic growth, business activity, or investor or business confidence; limitations on the availability of or increases in the cost of credit and capital; fluctuations in inflation or interest rates; uncertainties regarding fiscal and monetary policies; the timing and impact of changing governmental policies, including changes in guidance and interpretation by regulatory authorities; changes in trade policies by the U.S. or other countries; supply chain disruptions; consumer spending; employment levels; labor shortages; challenging labor market conditions; wage stagnation; U.S. government shutdowns; energy prices; home prices; commercial property values; bankruptcies and a default by a significant market participant or class of counterparties; natural disasters; climate change; epidemics; pandemics; terrorist attacks; acts of war; or a combination of these or other factors.

paragraphs: Total assets increased $11.3 billion, or 95.0%, to $23.2 billion as of December 31, 2025 from $11.9 billion as of December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily due to the assets assumed in the Transaction. The Transaction created a $23 billion Northeast franchise by combining Legacy Berkshire's stable, more rural funding base with Legacy Brookline's commercial lending focus in metro markets. The highly-complementary geographic footprints had minimal branch overlap ensuring minimal market disruption while also providing business diversification, fee income opportunities and improved competitive positioning. The Transaction also created meaningful near-term cost synergies while positioning the Company to benefit from future economies of scale.

Total loans and leases increased $8.3 billion, or 84.4%, to $18.0 billion as of December 31, 2025 from $9.8 billion as of December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily due to the loans assumed in the Transaction partially offset by the sales of $332.6 million of purchased mortgage loans acquired in the Transaction. The Company's commercial loan portfolios, which are comprised of commercial real estate loans and commercial loans and leases, totaled $14.0 billion, or 77.4% of total loans and leases as of December 31, 2025, an increase of $5.7 billion, or 69.8%, from $8.2 billion, or 84.1% of total loans and leases, as of December 31, 2024.

Total investment securities increased $0.8 billion, or 88.7%, to $1.7 billion as of December 31, 2025 from $0.9 billion as of December 31, 2024, primarily due to investment securities assumed in the Transaction partially offset by the sale of $176.4 million of the Legacy Berkshire's investment portfolio during the third quarter.

Cash and cash equivalents increased $1.5 billion, or 275.5%, to $2.0 billion as of December 31, 2025 from $0.5 billion as of December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily due to cash and equivalents assumed in the Transaction and an increased payroll deposit balance at December 31, 2025.

Total deposits increased $10.6 billion, or 119.2%, to $19.5 billion as of December 31, 2025 from $8.9 billion as of December 31, 2024, primarily due to the deposits assumed in the Transaction. Core deposits, which include demand checking, NOW, non-payroll money market and savings accounts, totaled $13.1 billion, or 67.0% of total deposits, as of December 31, 2025, an increase of $6.9 billion, or 112.6%, from $6.1 billion, or 69.1% of total deposits, as of December 31, 2024. Payroll deposits totaled $1.9 billion as of December 31, 2025, all of which was assumed in the Transaction. Certificate of deposit balances totaled $4.2 billion, or 21.3% of total deposits, as of December 31, 2025, an increase of $2.3 billion, or 120.5%, from $1.9 billion, or 21.2% of total deposits, as of December 31, 2024. Brokered deposit balances totaled $0.4 billion, or 2.1% of total deposits as of December 31, 2025, a decrease of $0.5 billion, or 52.8%, from $0.9 billion, or 9.8% of total deposits, as of December 31, 2024.

Total borrowed funds decreased $731.5 million, or 48.1%, to $788.4 million as of December 31, 2025 from $1.5 billion as of December 31, 2024 as combined liquidity as a result of the Transaction and the increase in deposits allowed for reduction in borrowings.

paragraphs: Beacon Financial Corporation, 一間 Delaware 公司，為 Beacon Bank & Trust 及其子公司與 Clarendon Private 的控股公司。
本公司提供廣泛的商業、企業與零售銀行服務，包括完整的現金管理產品、外匯服務、線上與行動銀行服務、消費者與住宅貸款以及財富管理服務。Clarendon Private 為美國證券交易委員會（SEC）登記的投資顧問公司。透過 Clarendon Private 與銀行的信託與投資部門，本公司為個人、家庭、基金會與捐助財團提供廣泛的財富管理服務，協助這些客戶達成其長期財務目標。
作為一間在新英格蘭與紐約擁有 147 間銀行分行的全方位金融機構，銀行及其子公司致力於透過完整的產品組合、優良的客戶服務與強大的風險管理，與合格客戶建立並深化長期的銀行關係。
本公司的總部與高階管理位於麻薩諸塞州波士頓 131 Clarendon Street，郵遞區號 02116，電話號碼為 617-425-4600。

於 2025 年 9 月 1 日，本公司完成與 Brookline Bancorp, Inc.（"Legacy Brookline"）的平權合併，依據 2024 年 12 月 16 日由本公司、Commerce Acquisition Sub, Inc. 與 Legacy Brookline 簽訂之合併協議與計畫（"Merger Agreement"）。於 2025 年 9 月 1 日，Commerce Acquisition Sub, Inc. 合併進 Legacy Brookline（"Merger"），隨即由 Legacy Brookline 合併進本公司（"Holdco Merger"），本公司為合併後之公司。本公司亦將其名稱由 Berkshire Hills Bancorp, Inc. 改為 Beacon Financial Corporation，並將其普通股於紐約證券交易所之股票代碼由 "BHLB" 改為 "BBT"。

於 2025 年 9 月 1 日，本公司完成與 Brookline Bancorp, Inc.（"Legacy Brookline"）的平權合併，依據 2024 年 12 月 16 日由本公司、Commerce Acquisition Sub, Inc. 與 Legacy Brookline 簽訂之合併協議與計畫（"Merger Agreement"）。於 2025 年 9 月 1 日，Commerce Acquisition Sub, Inc. 合併進 Legacy Brookline（"Merger"），隨即由 Legacy Brookline 合併進本公司（"Holdco Merger"），本公司為合併後之公司。本公司亦將其名稱由 Berkshire Hills Bancorp, Inc. 改為 Beacon Financial Corporation，並將其普通股於紐約證券交易所之股票代碼由 "BHLB" 改為 "BBT"。

於 Holdco 合併後，Berkshire Bank，為本公司之 wholly owned subsidiary，Bank Rhode Island，為 Legacy Brookline 之 wholly owned subsidiary，以及 PCSB Bank，為 Legacy Brookline 之 wholly owned subsidiary，各自與 Brookline Bank，為 Legacy Brookline 之 wholly owned subsidiary 合併，且 Brookline Bank 為存續銀行（稱為 "Bank Mergers"，與 Merger 及 Holdco Merger 合稱 "Transaction"）。於 Bank Mergers 期間，Brookline Bank 改為 Beacon Bank & Trust 名稱。
該 Transaction 被視為符合 ASC 805 之企業合併，並採用取得法進行會計處理。因此，於財務報導目的，Legacy Brookline 被視為買方，即使 Legacy Berkshire 為法律上之買方。因此，Legacy Brookline 之歷史財務報表成為合併後公司之歷史財務報表。

貸款及租賃組合增加 8.3 十億美元，或 84.4%，至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 18.0 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 9.8 十億美元。本公司商業貸款組合，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 14.0 十億美元，或總貸款及租賃的 77.4%，增加 5.7 十億美元，或 69.8%，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 8.2 十億美元，或總貸款及租賃的 84.1%。

總存款增加 10.6 十億美元，或 119.2%，至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 19.5 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 8.9 十億美元。核心存款，包括現金帳戶、NOW 帳戶、非薪資薪資市場帳戶及儲蓄帳戶，增加 112.6% 至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 13.1 十億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 6.1 十億美元。本公司核心存款於 2025 年 12 月 31 日為總存款的 67.0%，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 69.1% 減少。
銀行亦經營一個商業支付處理業務，服務區域及全國薪資服務機構客戶。這些薪資存款，包含在薪資市場帳戶中，會根據薪資週期每日波動數百萬美元。薪資存款，包含在合併財務報表的薪資市場帳戶中，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 1.9 十億美元，全部為交易中所假設的金額。

貸款及租賃損失備抵金增加 1.278 億美元，或 102.1%，至 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 2.528 億美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 1.251 億美元。貸款及租賃損失備抵金與總貸款及租賃的比率於 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 1.40%，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 1.28%。非 Performing 資產於 2025 年 12 月 31 日為 1.167 億美元，較 2024 年末的 0.705 億美元增加。非 Performing 資產於 2025 年 12 月 31 日為總資產的 0.50%，而 2024 年 12 月 31 日為 0.59%。
本公司面臨來自銀行及其他金融機構及金融服務供應商的強烈競爭。本公司在市場區域內，面對來自銀行及非銀行組織，包括傳統銀行、網際銀行、金融科技公司、財富管理公司及其他機構，在銀行及相關服務活動各方面的競爭。貸款產生的競爭因素包括產品提供、利率、提供的條件、提供的服務及地理位置。吸引及保留存款的競爭因素包括產品提供及回報率、便利的分行位置及自動提款機及線上存取帳戶。

paragraphs: 總資產增加 11.3 十億美元，或 95.0%，至 23.2 十億美元，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 11.9 十億美元相比。此增加主要係因交易中取得的資產。該交易透過將 Legacy Berkshire 穩定且較偏鄉的資金基礎與 Legacy Brookline 在都會區的商業貸款專注領域結合，創造出 23 十億美元的東北地區特許經營權。高度互補的地理版圖具有極少的分行重疊，確保了極小的市場幹擾，同時也提供了業務多元化、費用收入機會及改善的競爭地位。該交易也創造了顯著的短期成本協同效益，同時使本公司能受益於未來的規模經濟。

總貸款及租賃金額增加 8.3 十億美元，或 84.4%，至 18.0 十億美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 9.8 十億美元。此增加主要係因交易中所取得的貸款，部分抵銷 332.6 百萬美元的購入房貸貸款銷售。本公司之商業貸款組合，包含商業不動產貸款及商業貸款及租賃，總計為 14.0 十億美元，或佔總貸款及租賃金額的 77.4%，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 8.2 十億美元，或佔總貸款及租賃金額的 84.1%，增加 5.7 十億美元，或 69.8%。
總投資證券增加 0.8 十億美元，或 88.7%，至 1.7 十億美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 0.9 十億美元，主要係因交易中 assumed 的投資證券，部分抵銷第三季出售 Legacy Berkshire 投資組合 176.4 百萬美元
現金及現金等價物增加 1.5 十億美元，或 275.5%，至 2.0 十億美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 0.5 十億美元。此增加主要係因交易中取得的現金及等價物，以及 2025 年 12 月 31 日增加的薪資存款餘額。

總存款增加 10.6 十億美元，或 119.2%，至 19.5 十億美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 8.9 十億美元，主要係因交易中取得的存款。核心存款，包括現金帳戶、NOW 帳戶、非薪資貨幣市場帳戶及儲蓄帳戶，總計 13.1 十億美元，或總存款的 67.0%，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 6.1 十億美元，或總存款的 69.1%，增加了 6.9 十億美元，或 112.6%。薪資存款總計 1.9 十億美元，全部為交易中取得。存款憑證餘額總計 4.2 十億美元，或總存款的 21.3%，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 1.9 十億美元，或總存款的 21.2%，增加了 2.3 十億美元，或 120.5%。經紀存款餘額總計 0.4 十億美元，或總存款的 2.1%，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 0.9 十億美元，或總存款的 9.8%，減少 0.5 十億美元，或 52.8%。
總計負債資金減少 731.5 百萬美元，或 48.1%，至 788.4 百萬美元，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，相較於 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 1.5 十億美元，因交易及存款增加所致，允許減少借貸。

headings: 利率變動可能對我們的營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
我們可能因美國與全球經濟情勢的波動及財政、貨幣、貿易與規範政策的變動而受到不利影響。
通貨膨脹可能對我們的業務及客戶造成不利影響。
我們的業務可能因我們營運區域內經濟情勢的變動而受到不利影響。
若我們無法取得資本市場資金、出現持續的淨存款流出，或借款成本增加，將對我們的流動性與競爭地位造成負面影響。
我們在金融服務業面臨著顯著且不斷增加的競爭。
新產品、服務與科技的開發可能對我們增加額外成本，並使我們面臨更高的營運風險。
美國貿易政策的變動，包括課徵關稅與報復性關稅，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成不利影響。
若本公司針對信用損失的撥備不足以涵蓋實際的貸款及租賃損失，則本公司獲利可能減少。
本公司貸款及租賃組合包含商業不動產抵押貸款及商業貸款及租賃，包括設備租賃，這些貸款通常較其他類型貸款風險更高。
本公司貸款組閤中有一部分為貸款參與，這些貸款可能較本公司自行發放的貸款有更高的損失風險，因為本公司並非主貸人，且對信用監控的控制力有限。
本公司在進行貸款銷售時，可能面臨多種風險。
44 美商商業資本公司的 SBA 7(a) 貸款業務依賴美國聯邦政府，本公司面臨與發放 SBA 貸款相關的特定風險。
與本公司貸款業務相關的環境責任可能導致損失。
本公司投資證券的公允價值可能因超出本公司控制範疇的因素而波動。
美國政府證券若被一個或多個信用評級機構降級，可能對本公司營運、獲利及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
存款流失或存款結構變化可能會提高我們的資金成本。
機構資金來源可能不足以在存款到期時取代存款，並支撐我們的營運及未來成長。
FHLB 的表現或財務狀況惡化可能會限制我們的資金需求，並可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
其他金融機構的健全性可能會對我們產生不利影響。
我們償還債務及發放紅利的能力取決於銀行的資本分配，而這些分配受到監管限制及其他限制。
我們的聲譽受損可能會嚴重影響我們的業務，包括我們的競爭地位及業務前景。
我們可能無法吸引並留住合格的關鍵員工，這可能會對我們的業務前景，包括我們的競爭地位及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們面臨持續增長的資料安全風險，包括我們所維護的客戶相關資訊。
我們可能無法成功實施未來資訊科技系統的改進，這可能會對我們的業務運作及獲利造成不利影響。
我們依賴其他公司提供我們業務基礎設施的關鍵零組件。
我們可能因風險管理流程及策略不當而產生重大損失。
我們的內部控制、作業程序及政策可能失效或遭繞過。
稅法及規範的變更，以及對稅法及規範解釋的差異，可能會對我們的財務報表造成不利影響。
天然災害、恐怖攻擊、未來疫情及其他外部事件可能對我們的業務造成損害。
我們的財務報表部分基於假設及估計，若假設及估計錯誤，可能會導致未來出現意外損失。
會計準則的變更可能難以預測，並可能對我們記錄及報告財務狀況與營運成果的方式產生重大影響。
本公司可能須要減記商譽及其他與併購相關之可辨認智慧財產權資產。
本公司營運於高度管制之產業，法律及法規，或其變更，可能限制或限制本公司活動，並可能對本公司營運產生重大不利影響。
本公司受多項法律規範，旨在保護消費者，包括社區再投資法案及公平貸款法規，若未遵守這些法規，可能導致種種處罰。
本公司即使因非故意或未預料之非遵守，仍可能面臨執行行動。
本公司面臨重大法律風險，來自於監管調查及程序，以及來自私人提告之行動。
美國聯邦儲備銀行（FRB）可能要求本公司投入資本資源以支持銀行。
本公司受嚴格資本要求之限制，可能對權益回報率產生不利影響，或要求追加資本籌集，或限制支付股息或買回股票之能力。
本公司可能無法實現交易預期之效益。

paragraphs: 在決定投資本公司或維持或增加投資前，您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，以及本報告及本公司其他向 SEC 提交的文件中所包含的其他資訊。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非本公司唯一面臨的風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能影響本公司業務。如果任何已知或未知的風險與不確定性實際發生，將可能嚴重影響本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果。在此情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌，您可能喪失投資。
與本公司業務與產業相關的風險

本公司合併後的營運成果在很大程度上取決於淨利息收入，即 (i) 對於產生利息的資產（如貸款、租賃及證券）所產生的利息收入，與 (ii) 對於產生利息的負債（如存款及借入資金）所產生的利息支出之間的差額。因此，本公司獲利與成長會受到利率的重大影響，而利率會受到總體經濟狀況（包括國內與國際）的影響，也會受到資本市場事件以及美國與聯邦儲備銀行（FRB）貨幣與財政政策的影響。這些政策的性質與時間點及其對本公司影響無法控制，且極其難以預測。利率上升也可能對本公司營運成果產生負面影響，因為這會降低借款人的還款能力，這不僅可能導致貸款違約、財產拍賣與呆帳增加，也可能需要進一步提高貸款損失準備金。

美國與全球經濟在近年來經歷了波動，並可能在可預見的未來繼續經歷波動。不利或不確定的經濟狀況可能由經濟成長、商業活動或投資者與企業信心下降；信貸與資本可得性減少或成本上升；通貨膨脹或利率波動；財政與貨幣政策的不確定性；政府政策變動的時間與影響，包括監管當局的指引與解釋變動；美國或其他國家貿易政策的變動；供應鏈中斷；消費者支出；就業水平；勞動力短缺；困難的勞動市場條件；工資停滯；美國政府停擺；能源價格；房價；商業不動產價值；破產以及重要市場參與者或對手方類別的違約；天然災害；氣候變遷；疫情；大流行；恐怖攻擊；戰爭行為；或這些或其他因素的組合所造成。
波動的業務與經濟條件可能對本公司業務產生不利影響，包括以下項目：
• 投資者可能對整體股市與金融服務業股票的信心降低，這可能會對本公司股票價格造成向下壓力，並導致市場估值下降
